restyle: Redraw the first image in the cut-paper collage style of the second image, like a 1950s children's picture book made from coloured paper: every shape is a flat piece of cut or torn coloured paper with a subtle paper grain and slightly irregular hand-cut edges, simple drawn lines for stone courses, roof slates and planks, tiny soft shadows where paper layers overlap, and a limited warm palette of honey stone, cream, sage and olive greens, duck-egg blue sky, mustard, tomato red and teal. Keep the composition of the first image identical: every building, roof, chimney, door, window, sign bracket, lamp, bench, table, fence, wall, gate, tree, path, bridge, water and hill must stay in exactly the same place, at the same size and in the same shape, so the new picture lines up when laid over the old one. Do not add or remove anything. Doors and window frames are clean, bold, clearly separate pieces of paper. Paths, pavements, lawns, cobbles, platforms and other ground surfaces are made of a few large, calm pieces of paper with only faint drawn joints, so that small objects lying on them would be easy to see. No people, no text, no lettering, no litter. Wide 3:2 landscape, full-bleed, no border or frame.
